title: Co-evolving proactive telecare: a mixed methods study on the implementation and use of technology to support remote monitoring and care at home
summary:
Background and study aims
Background: Technology-enabled care (TEC) is viewed by many as at least a partial solution to the complex challenges of delivering social care. Telecare (continuous remote monitoring for safety and wellbeing using sensors and personal trigger alarms) has been mainstream within social care for decades. However, most telecare technologies commissioned in the UK provide a ‘reactive’ service, based on alerts triggered by the person’s need for assistance (e.g. pendant alarm, fall detector). The last decade has seen a proliferation of digital devices that offer potential to expand scope for more ‘proactive’ telecare; that is, the use of multifunctional digital devices to support activity monitoring using sensors and outreach contact through ICT (information and communication technology). Proactive telecare offers potential advantages to service users (e.g. more personalised support, remaining home for longer) and the social care system (e.g. increased capacity, reduced care support needs). But concerns have been expressed about the impact on service access (e.g. digital exclusion) and quality of care (e.g. replacing in-person contact). There remain significant technical, practical and regulatory challenges to implementation.

Aim: To study and inform the implementation of proactive telecare, and draw transferable lessons on the nature of such services and how they can be effectively used and embedded within social care.

Who can participate?
•	Service users and their family/informal carers receiving technology-enabled care within the participating case sites
•	Staff and system stakeholders involved in providing and supporting of  technology-enabled care within the participating case sites

What does the study involve?
Participants will be interviewed about their views and experiencing using, or supporting someone with, technology-enabled care. Interviews with service users and their family/informal carers will be conducted in their own home on up to three occasions. They may also be provided with everyday artefacts (e.g. diaries, digital camera) to document aspects of their life that they would like to talk about with the researcher. Interviews with staff and other system stakeholders will be conducted over video call or at their place of work, to talk about their role and experience using such technology within routine care practice, as well as the organisational challenges and changes involved. 

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
The participants will not benefit directly from the findings of the study, though it will inform how social care providers can support users more effectively through the use of technology. There are no identified risks. However, the time commitment and the process of having a researcher speaking with them at home can be potentially burdensome. The date and time for the interviews will be completely up to the participant. 

Where is the study run from?
The study is led by University of Oxford, in collaboration with London School of Economics (LSE) and King's College London. Data collection, including service user/carer and staff/stakeholder interviews will be conducted in three participating case sites, including local authorities and social care organisations providing technology to support proactive and preventative approaches to care.  

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
March 2026 to May 2028.

Who is funding the study?
NIHR Research Programme for Social Care

Who is the main contact?
Joe Wherton, joseph.wherton@phc.ox.ac.uk

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Service user participants and informal carers/family members:
1. Over 18 years of age
2. Receiving care from participating services, or  supporting/living with the service user
3. Able to provide informed consent.

Staff participants:
1. Implementing or using proactive telecare, or  whose work is affected by the introduction of such technology/services. 

National stakeholder participants:
1. Role in the  innovation, policymaking or regulation of proactive telecare
Exclusion criteria:
1. Under 18 years of age
2. Lacks capacity to consent
